state: Pinned firmware bytes match upstream Tegra210 L4T-r32.7.6 firmware; B01 native execution not tested

license.readme_scope: External binary is not MIT and is not committed with the source. Section2.1.2 includes an OSI-open-source-operating-system condition on redistribution; Windows redistribution rights must be resolved before including this blob in a public Windows package.

nvidia_manifest.finding: Names tegra21x/nvhost_nvdec020_ns.fw as the no-bootloader NVDEC firmware; this older manifest is a naming/selection reference, not proof of byte identity with R32.7.6.

findings: The vendor t21_nvdec_info encodes NVDEC2.0; no separateB01 firmware selection branch appears in the reviewed t210/nvdec files. Absence of a branch is not proof of B01 execution.

The vendor no-bootloader branch selects nvhost_nvdec020_ns.fw. The bootloader-enabled path instead selects debug/prod bootloader and firmware using SCP state and WPR information. Do not mix these loading contracts.

Linuxv6.8 selects nvidia/tegra210/nvdec.bin for nvidia,tegra210-nvdec and uses the Falcon path without the newer-SoC stream-ID setup. Its physical/IOMMU ownership still comes from Linux and is not inherited by Windows.

Existing loader uses256-byte Falcon transfers, one OS-data base adjustment, relative code/data offsets, then STARTCPU/idle polling. These steps match the reviewed single-image Falcon path; runtime DMA, security state and actual completion remain unverified.
limits: The actual installed Noble kernel build/config, nvdec_enabled boot argument and selected firmware have not been retrieved in this round; the pinned vendor source is a reference only.
No actual Windows NVDEC SCP/firmware-idle/client-route measurements or decoded pixels exist yet.
Do not bypass secure/WPR firmware selection or assume Linux memory isolation equals the Windows route.
Firmware provenance does not validate the local scratch capacity fix on hardware.
